security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline examples, and repository authoring guidance. I found no evidence of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, malware behavior, or unauthorized network activity in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: Search `microsoft-docs` MCP for current API patterns:
- **Frontmatter**: `name` and `description`. The description is the trigger mechanism.
| `scripts/` | Deterministic operations | Same code rewritten repeatedly |
| `references/` | Detailed patterns | API docs, schemas, detailed guides |
Skills are organized by **language** and **product area** in the `skills/` directory via symlinks.
| `data` | Storage, Cosmos DB, Tables, Data Lake | `azure-cosmos-py`, `azure-storage-blob-py` |
| `messaging` | Event Hubs, Service Bus, Event Grid | `azure-eventhub-py`, `azure-servicebus-py` |
1. Search `microsoft-docs` MCP for current API patterns
After creating the skill in `.github/skills/`, create a symlink in the appropriate category:
- Remove the `azure-` prefix and language suffix
- `forbidden_patterns` — common mistakes that must NOT appear
- `mock_response` — complete, working code that passes all checks
- Update total skill count (line ~73: `> N skills in...`)
- Update Skill Explorer link count (line ~15: `Browse all N skills`)
- Update language section count (e.g., `> N skills • suffix: -py`)
- Update test coverage summary (line ~622: `**N skills with N test scenarios**`)
This updates `docs-site/src/data/skills.json` which feeds the Astro-based docs site.
This outputs to `docs/` which is served by GitHub Pages.
| `messaging` | Event Hubs, Service Bus, Event Grid | `azure-eventhub-py`, `azure-servicebus-py` |

content.value_statement: Developers need reusable skill guidance for Azure SDK and Microsoft Foundry work. This skill provides structure, examples, testing patterns, and documentation checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains required SKILL.md frontmatter and body structure.
Defines a recommended section order for Azure SDK skills.
Shows authentication examples using DefaultAzureCredential across languages.
Guides authors to verify current SDK patterns from Microsoft documentation.
Describes acceptance criteria and scenario testing for generated skills.
Documents repository categorization with language and product area symlinks.
limitations: Requires the user to provide an SDK package, documentation URL, or repository reference.
Focuses on Azure SDK and Microsoft Foundry skills, not every possible domain.
Does not include executable validation scripts or automated generators.
Examples may need adaptation for repository-specific layouts and test harnesses.

use_cases.title: Create a New Azure SDK Skill
use_cases.description: Use the guide to plan frontmatter, workflow sections, authentication examples, references, and tests for a new SDK skill.

use_cases.title: Standardize Skill Contributions
use_cases.description: Apply consistent naming, categorization, and acceptance criteria before adding new skills to a shared repository.

use_cases.title: Update Existing Foundry Skills
use_cases.description: Refresh examples against current Microsoft documentation and improve coverage for common authentication and import patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner author with a known SDK package.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a new Azure SDK skill for [SDK package]. Include the required SKILL.md sections and user context questions.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Skill Instructions
prompt_templates.scenario: Author has documentation and wants a first draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SKILL.md draft for [SDK package] using [documentation URL]. Include authentication, core workflow, cleanup, and reference file suggestions.

prompt_templates.title: Add Test Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Maintainer needs acceptance criteria and scenarios.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed skill and produce acceptance criteria plus scenario test ideas for import paths, authentication, async usage, and common mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Repository Integration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced contributor preparing a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Azure SDK skill for repository readiness. Check naming, category placement, reference organization, documentation updates, and test coverage gaps.

output_examples.input: Create a skill plan for an Azure AI Agents Python SDK skill.
output: Recommended skill name and trigger description.
Section outline covering installation, environment variables, authentication, workflow, cleanup, and references.
Suggested acceptance criteria for imports, client creation, tool use, and error handling.

output_examples.input: Review an existing Foundry skill for readiness.
output: Findings about missing documentation verification, weak trigger text, and incomplete test scenarios.
Concrete changes for frontmatter, reference files, category links, and README catalog updates.

output_examples.input: Design test scenarios for an Azure Storage skill.
output: Scenario names for basic client setup, pagination, long-running operations, and invalid credential patterns.
Expected and forbidden patterns that can guide a repository test harness.

best_practices: Start with current Microsoft documentation and verify SDK version-specific API patterns.
Keep SKILL.md concise and move detailed workflows into reference files.
Include acceptance criteria that catch wrong imports, unsafe credentials, and missing cleanup.
anti_patterns: Creating an SDK skill without a package name, documentation URL, or repository reference.
Hardcoding credentials or recommending API keys when managed identity patterns are available.
Skipping tests, category placement, or catalog updates after adding a skill.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps authors create or update skills for Azure SDKs and Microsoft Foundry services.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete skill automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides structure, examples, and review criteria that an agent can apply during authoring.

faq.question: What input should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the SDK package name, Microsoft Learn documentation URL, or repository reference.

faq.question: Which tools can use the skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover non-Azure skills?
faq.answer: Only partially. Its strongest guidance is for Azure SDK and Microsoft Foundry skill patterns.

faq.question: How should authors test a new skill?
faq.answer: Create acceptance criteria and scenario tests that verify imports, authentication, workflow behavior, and common anti-patterns.
